          Chelsea's Attack Fires, Arsenal Frustrated Again, Man City Escape Hayes Lane: Five WSL Talking Points from MD8
        
      
                          
                      Nov 3, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Chelsea and Manchester City kept pace at the top, Arsenal stumbled again, and Tottenham got back to winning ways. We break down the biggest talking points from another weekend of WSL action

Chelsea and Manchester City kept pace at the top of the WSL, though only one title contender enjoyed a comfortable afternoon. While Chelsea cruised to a six-goal victory over Charlton, City were pushed all the way by an ambitious London City Lionesses side that delivered one of the performances of the season despite ultimately coming away empty-handed.

Elsewhere, Arsenal's recent signs of recovery were halted by another frustrating draw at the Emirates, while north London rivals Tottenham ended a three-match losing streak to get back to winning ways. Manchester United extended their unbeaten run in all competitions to 10 matches, but were unable to find a way past a resilient Everton side.

At the other end of the table, the struggles continue for the newly promoted clubs. Charlton were on the receiving end of Chelsea's latest attacking masterclass, while Birmingham City remain in search of their first league victory of the campaign.
Here are the biggest talking points from this weekend's WSL action.

It seems as if it's always the same story with Renée Slegers' side this season, as Arsenal were held 1-1 at the Emirates. In doing so, they became the first team in WSL history to draw four consecutive home games.

After back-to-back wins had offered supporters a glimmer of hope that the tide might finally be turning, Sunday's result felt like a familiar frustration. Arsenal dominated possession but struggled to turn that control into genuine threat before Aston Villa nicked a goal with their only shot of the game.

In fact, the Gunners' 90.9% passing accuracy was their second highest on record in a WSL match and their best at home, yet they created just two big chances, their lowest tally at the Emirates this season.

It was the first time in the competition’s history that an away team has scored with their only shot of a game. Remarkably, all three instances of that happening overall have now come at the expense of Arsenal: Bristol City in May 2023 and Aston Villa in March 2024. Yet this match was the first time the team with just one shot did not go on to lose.

Chasity Grant‘s opener in the 25th minute once again highlighted Arsenal's fragility in transition. The goal continued a worrying trend for Arsenal. Their opponents have now scored with their first shot in each of the Gunners' last two WSL matches, while they have conceded the opening goal in three consecutive home league games within the same season for the first time since 2015.

Aston Villa's 0.07 expected goals (xG) was the fifth-lowest total by a team in WSL history to avoid defeat. Yet, as they also demonstrated in a 1-1 draw against Brighton earlier this season, despite an xG of just 0.03, the Villans have developed a knack for staying in games.

Meanwhile, Alessia Russo’s last-ditch leveller, spared Arsenal from what would have been another chorus of boos around the Emirates. The goal, created by Stina Blackstenius, was only the fourth time the pair have combined for a WSL goal.

The hourglass was already running low for Slegers a few weeks ago, and with Arsenal down in seventh, the sand is disappearing fast. Their tally of 10 points is only better than their return of eight at this stage in 2014.

For Chelsea, it was goals galore in south-east London as the Blues ran riot at The Valley, recording their second-biggest WSL victory under Sonia Bompastor after the 7-0 demolition of Crystal Palace in September 2024.

It took less than three minutes for the visitors to break through. Nathalie Björn rose highest to meet Katie McCabe‘s delivery, with Charlton conceding the earliest goal of their WSL history. It was a notable moment for McCabe too, who registered assists in consecutive league appearances for the first time since November 2021.

The warning signs were immediate and Charlton had little answer to Chelsea's relentless pressure. By the 10-minute mark the Blues had doubled their lead and from there the contest quickly turned into one-way traffic as Bompastor's side produced one of the most dominant attacking displays of the season.
Chelsea finished with chances worth 6.37 expected goals, their highest xG total ever recorded in a WSL away game on Opta's records (since 2017-18).
They attempted 36 shots, the most by a Chelsea side in the competition since September 2020 against Bristol City (39) and Chelsea's highest tally ever in an away league match.

Melvine Malard continued her rich vein of form. The French forward scored twice and was unfortunate not to complete a hat-trick after seeing another effort ruled out for offside. It's the second time in her WSL career that she has scored braces in consecutive league games, having previously done so for Manchester United in September 2025.

There were personal milestones elsewhere. Aggie Beever-Jones swept home to end a 13-month league goal drought, while summer signing Giulia Dragoni opened her Chelsea account with a composed finish, becoming the youngest Italian ever to score in the WSL and only the fourth in the competition's history.
